text: P0-A FINDING (verified by execution, not inspection) + A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE. (1) THE MARKER TRAP IS IN THE PAYMENT GATE. server/research/early-access/release/canonical-payment-eligibility.ts:214 compositionResolvedFromSpecification decides compositionResolved with /split pending|pending split|\btbd\b|unresolved/i. Executed: the WORKBOOK spec 'CJC-1295 WITH DAC + IPAMORELIN 5 mg total (split pending)' gives resolved=false (refused, correct); the CANONICAL spec from your reviewed config, 'CJC-1295 WITH DAC + IPAMORELIN 5 mg total', gives resolved=TRUE and passes the gate. The marker is stripped in the canonical spec - correctly, a customer should not read our internal uncertainty in a product name - so the helper returns the wrong answer for the one row it exists to catch, the moment the reconciled artifact lands. The GATE is sound: it checks held, and checks composition BEFORE price, which is the right order. Only the interim helper is wrong, and the file already says it is interim. FIX: derive compositionResolved from the reviewed record rather than from text. server/research/master-offerings/reviewed-holds.ts already answers exactly this, keyed on the canonical specification: isFormulationHeld(spec, reviewedHeldSpecifications()). That file is not my lease so I am reporting, not editing. PATTERN WORTH NAMING: this is the third instance of one assumption - I shipped it and fixed it at ba2c52b, lane4 fixed it in the acceptance matrix after my warning, and it is here. Any rule that reads product COPY to infer a product FACT dies the moment the copy is cleaned up for customers. Worth a standing rule rather than three separate fixes. (2) CORRECTION TO MY COLLAPSED-PAIR ADVICE. I told you price and classification are ONE choice. That is true of the raw workbook rows and NOT true of the reviewed reconciliation, which is where the decision is encoded: a merge's canonical block declares product, specification, family, channel and retailPriceCents as SEPARATE fields. So the config can keep GRP-0426 (RUO, directly orderable) as the survivor and simply state retailPriceCents 6250. The founder's 62.50/107.50 override does NOT force 109/29 - that only follows if it is implemented by swapping survivors. s10's reading (RUO row survives, price changes, 111-direct preserved) is both cheaper and closer to what he was actually choosing, since he was shown a price recommendation and picked a price. Two numbers in the config plus a production price adjudication flip. My warning was worth making because it got the question asked explicitly instead of inferred, but please do not let it push the launch toward making two products unorderable. Still not regenerating until he confirms which implementation.
